items.title: Ek request ka safar: click se jawab tak, Phase 1 ka poora map
items.one_idea: One tap on a link is one journey: the browser asks DNS for the address, opens a TCP connection, adds TLS for HTTPS, sends an HTTP request, a load balancer picks one of several servers, and the response comes back; each stop adds latency, and any stop with no backup is a single point of failure that hurts availability.
items.spoken_hook: Request जाने से पहले ही, आठ चक्कर लग जाते हैं।
items.hook_formula: surprising_fact: a counted, sourced fact about the viewer's own click (MDN's own tally of eight round trips before the HTTPS request is sent), plain statement, no question after it
items.hook_10s: Request जाने से पहले ही, आठ चक्कर लग जाते हैं। ये MDN की गिनती है, एक simple HTTPS page के लिए। आज एक click का पूरा सफ़र देखते हैं: DNS से लेकर server और वापस, हर stop पर क्या होता है और कहाँ टूट सकता है। [frame 0: a phone on the left, a server on the right, eight small arrows going back and forth between them before a single page card appears]

items.visual_idea: One fixed horizontal road: phone, DNS book, a TCP handshake of three arrows, a padlock for TLS, a load balancer fanning to three servers, then the page card returning along the same road. A stopwatch ticks on every stop (latency adds up) and a red marker shows which stop is a single point of failure, then a second copy appears beside it.
items.everyday_anchor: Ordering food on a delivery app: look up the restaurant's address, call and confirm, hand over the order securely, a dispatcher picks a rider, the food comes back; any step with no backup stops the order.
items.example: EXAMPLE: a page request passes DNS, TCP, TLS, load balancer and one app server; if each stop is up 99.9% and they are in a row, the whole path is up about 99.5% (0.999^5), arithmetic labelled EXAMPLE, not a real company's number.
facts_to_verify: MDN How browsers work: TLS needs five more round trips and 'after eight round trips' the browser can make the request; say it is MDN's simplified count for an HTTPS page, real counts depend on TLS version and reused connections
DNS lookup returns the IP address; usually cached after the first request (MDN How browsers work)
TCP three-way handshake SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK, after DNS and before TLS (MDN TCP handshake)
HTTP is client/server, the browser always starts the request; proxies between can do load balancing (MDN HTTP overview)
load balancer sends each request to one backend server (Wikipedia Load balancing)
SPOF definition (Wikipedia); availability = ability to access the service (Wikipedia High availability)
series availability 0.999^5 is EXAMPLE arithmetic: recompute and show it
Cloudflare and other CDN pages not fetched; do not claim anything about CDN or caching speed-ups
